verdict.rationale: Appwrite Cloud documents project environments such as `staging`, each with its own resources and users, selected per request via the X-Appwrite-Environment header. That lets testing run in a separate environment without touching production data. Self-hosting a full local containerized instance is a second documented test path, and a community user noted the containerized setup eases testing. missing for 10: environments live inside the production project rather than as a dedicated sandbox tenancy, no documentation on seeding or cloning test data, no hands-on corroboration of environment isolation, and environment support is documented for Cloud only.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: On Appwrite Cloud, a project can have environments, such as `staging`, each with its own resources and users
The client sends the environment's ID in the `X-Appwrite-Environment` header with every request
You can install and run Appwrite on any operating system that can run a Docker CLI.
